activities.title: Build EX-004
activities.description: Build activity for: Emergency repair orders from the plant must continue to be sent nightly to OrivaBuy until the transition service agreement ends.
activities.source_rationale: KB-P2P-001 explicitly states that 'Feeding requisitions or orders to an application outside the ERP system on a schedule' is typically beyond the standard. The requirement is to send emergency repair orders nightly to OrivaBuy, which constitutes feeding orders to an external application on a schedule. The standard provides no object, process, or extension point for this scheduled outbound transmission, so the entire transport mechanism, mapping, scheduling, and error handling must be built, placing it in the Development tier.

activities.title: Build EX-008
activities.description: Build activity for: Automatically load supplier risk scores from the Nivora Risk Hub spreadsheet, despite it being a carve-out-specific, temporary system.
activities.source_rationale: The standard does not provide a field or mechanism to load externally maintained risk scores (KB-MD-007: 'no delivered field fed by that source ... requires a built interface with its own scheduling, error handling, and monitoring'). Loading partner attributes on a schedule from an outside application is beyond the standard (KB-MD-001: 'Loading partner attributes on a schedule from an application outside the ERP system'). Therefore, building an automated load from the Nivora Risk Hub spreadsheet requires new development (Development).

activities.title: Build EX-012
activities.description: Build activity for: Orders placed through the legacy Virello customer portal by strategic customers must be automatically converted into NewCo sales orders without manual re-keying during the first six months.
activities.source_rationale: The requirement is to automatically convert orders from a legacy portal into sales orders without manual re-keying. KB-O2C-006 states that when a sending portal uses a payload not in a standard format, 'the standard has no way to interpret it' and that 'Converting a portal-specific payload into sales orders without manual re-entry' is typically beyond the standard. KB-O2C-001 also confirms that creating sales orders from an unrecognized payload format is beyond the standard. Therefore, this requires building the receiving endpoint, mapping, error handling, and monitoring—new development.

activities.title: Build EX-019
activities.description: Build activity for: Send a nightly custom file to the Auralis Separation Ledger with Day-1 balances for treasury reconciliation outside the ERP during the first two quarters.
activities.source_rationale: The requirement is to build a recurring custom file for an external system (Auralis Separation Ledger) with a specific layout for Day-1 balances. According to KB-R2R-004, a nightly file whose layout, naming, and delivery are dictated by a receiving application is not delivered; producing it is a build. KB-XC-002 states that any bespoke interface to a named external application is a project deliverable, including scheduled extracts with custom formats. KB-R2R-001 lists recurring bespoke extracts as beyond the standard. The standard provides no object, process, or extension point for this end-to-end feed; therefore, it requires development.

activities.title: Build EX-024
activities.description: Build activity for: An upload from the SeltraBridge archive must bring over product drawings and link them to product records.
activities.source_rationale: The requirement is for an upload from an external archive (SeltraBridge) to bring product drawings and link them to products in bulk. According to KB-MD-008, the standard delivers attachment service and document management with object links, but 'Moving a large body of drawings out of an external archive, deciding from the archive's metadata which product each drawing belongs to, and creating the object links in bulk is a build: the reading of the archive, the matching rule, the error handling for unmatched files, and the rerun behaviour are all project deliverables.' KB-MD-004 also states that attaching externally sourced documents to products in bulk according to project linkage rules is beyond the standard. Furthermore, KB-XC-002 confirms that a project-specific connection to a named external application is a build. Therefore, the requirement falls into Development because the standard provides no pre-built interface for this specific archive extraction and bulk linking with project-defined matching.
